text.p: The European Parliament has approved the Europe Agreement with Slovenia while requesting some amendments.

It first adopted a report by Ulpu Iivari of the foreign affairs committee which said the signing of the Europe Agreement on June 10, 1996, will allow Slovenia to catch up with other east European countries in preparing for EU membership.

The agreement, which sets up a political dialogue between the EU and Slovenia as well as a free trade area after a six year transitional period, was reached after Italy and Slovenia settled a longstanding property rights dispute.

The Parliament adopted a second report on Thursday by Bernd Posselt of the external economic relations committee urging the EU to help fund large Slovenian transport projects and link them into trans-European networks.
The report also urged the EU to provide aid to help frontier towns, formerly dependent on customs and import/export business, to convert to other environmentally friendly activities.
